issues.legal_issue: Compulsory acquisition for a private cooperative housing society to allot plots to its members is not transformed into a public-purpose acquisition merely because the society is cooperative; the acquisition must fall within the statutory route and purposes applicable to it.
material_facts: The society was registered under cooperative-society legislation and sought land to develop and allot plots to its members for building houses.
There was no group housing scheme approved by the State, and the acquisition was for the society’s members rather than an identified public housing programme.
The agreement made under the company-acquisition provisions was given up, and the acquisition did not satisfy the mandatory requirements applicable to acquisition for a company.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition for allotment of plots to the society’s members was a private purpose, not a public purpose. It could not be sustained through the public-purpose route, and the acquisition provisions applicable to companies could not be used to authorize a private purpose outside their permitted categories.
issues.legal_principle: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 distinguishes public-purpose acquisition from acquisition for a company under Part VII. Sections 39–41 impose mandatory requirements for company acquisitions, including prior consent and an agreement, while sections 44-A and 44-B protect the purposes and public interest underlying such acquisitions. The court applied the statutory scheme, including sections 3(e) and 3(f), and relied on Jhandulal v. State of Punjab for the distinction between public-purpose and company acquisitions.

rule.if: compulsory_land_acquisition and private_cooperative_housing_purpose and land_intended_for_member_plots and no_genuine_public_benefit

predicates.compulsory_land_acquisition: The government sought to acquire privately owned land compulsorily.
predicates.private_cooperative_housing_purpose: A private cooperative housing organization sought the land for its housing activities.
predicates.land_intended_for_member_plots: The land was intended to be divided or allotted as plots to the organization’s members.
predicates.no_genuine_public_benefit: The acquisition was not shown to serve a public housing programme or another benefit to the community generally.

issues.definition: When compulsory acquisition is sought for a private cooperative housing purpose, the land is for members’ plots, and no genuine public benefit is shown, the acquisition is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A nominal contribution from public funds does not by itself convert an acquisition serving a private purpose into a public-purpose acquisition; the acquisition’s true purpose must be assessed in its circumstances.
material_facts: The State contributed Rs 100 for each acquisition declaration, while the land was sought for a private cooperative society’s members.
The members shown on the record included professionals and businesspeople, and some were alleged to own more than one house.
The State had not adequately considered the private purpose and the intended beneficiaries before accepting the report and making the nominal contributions.
issues.conclusion: The nominal contributions did not make the acquisition one for a public purpose. In the circumstances, the declarations were a colourable exercise of the acquisition power.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a contribution from public funds is sufficient depends on the circumstances; a nominal contribution is not automatically sufficient and may indicate colourable use of power. The court relied on Somavanti v. State of Punjab, Indrajit C. Parekh v. State of Gujarat, Bai Malimabu v. State of Gujarat, Land Acquisition Collector v. Durga Pada Mukherjee, Manubhai Jehtalal Patel v. State of Gujarat, and Jhandulal v. State of Punjab. Those authorities require examination of the actual purpose and the surrounding facts rather than treating a token contribution as conclusive.

rule.if: compulsory_land_acquisition and nominal_public_contribution and private_member_benefit and government_did_not_examine_actual_purpose

predicates.compulsory_land_acquisition: The government sought to acquire privately owned land compulsorily.
predicates.nominal_public_contribution: The government contributed only a nominal amount toward the acquisition cost.
predicates.private_member_benefit: The intended beneficiaries were members of a private organization rather than the public generally.
predicates.government_did_not_examine_actual_purpos: The government did not adequately consider who would benefit from the acquisition and whether its purpose was genuinely public.

issues.definition: When a compulsory acquisition is supported only by a nominal public contribution, benefits a private organization’s members, and the government has not examined its actual purpose, the acquisition is a colourable exercise of power.
